Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
Bench: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7521 of 2023
Applicant :- Irfan

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ali Qambar Zaidi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.
Heard Sri Ali Qambar Zaidi, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Chandan Agarwal, learned AGA for State.

2. Applicant-Irfan has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 252 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Jarcha, District Gautambudh Nagar, after rejection of his bail application vide order dated 02.02.2023 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO Act), Second,
Gautambudh Nagar.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO Act), Second,
Gautambudh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Victim, a married woman, aged about 30 years, having two children, herself lodged FIR against applicant herein on 29.12.2022 that applicant forcefully entered in her house, assaulted her and thereafter raped her.

It was also alleged that for last one year applicant was regularly harassing,
abusing and threatening victim and even he has recorded a video while she was changing clothes

Irfan vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35180003/
1 and threatening to viral it as well as to murder her husband and children.
Victim further alleged that when she raised alarm her mother-in-law and younger brother of her husband came and applicant ran away.
Since she was under threat, FIR was lodged after six days when her husband came back from his place of working, which was outside the city.
4. Learned counsel for applicant vehemently submits that it is a case of false implication.
Applicant is a neighbour of victim and earlier there was dispute with regard to throwing of garbage which was objected by applicant, therefore, he has been falsely implicated in present case.
Learned counsel further submits that delay of five days in lodging of FIR remained unexplained.
Alleged video was not recovered.
Narration of manner of occurrence has material difference in FIR and statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
Even statement of alleged eye witnesses were also differs.
Medical examination does not corroborate prosecution case and narration of facts with regard to recording of video also differs in statements.
Applicant is a 25 years old young boy having no criminal history and is languishing in jail since 29.12.2022, therefore, he may be released on bail.

5. Learned AGA has vehemently opposed bail and referred medical examination of victim that there was a bruise blue on left forearm and also refers the eye witness account, i.e., mother-in-law of victim, who has stated that on hearing hue and cry of victim when she reached near door of room she witnessed applicant holding his pants and only wearing necker.
She also states that applicant was saying that victim belongs to her only.
Learned AGA also refers statement of Dewar (a handicapped person) of victim that when he was returning towards his house, he saw applicant running away from his house.
Lastly it is submitted that delay of five days may not be considered as an adverse factor since husband of victim was working out of city and in cases of rape there is also a fear of social disgrace.
6. LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

sentences.text: In the present case, FIR was lodged by victim herself.
There is merit in the argument of learned AGA that delay of five days may not be considered to be adverse factor considering background of victim and apprehension of social disgrace.
8. There are eye witness account of mother-in-law of victim, who has seen applicant running out of the room in his necker carrying pant in his hands.
He was shouting that victim belongs only to him.
Said version prima facie corroborates by statement of Dewar of victim, who also saw applicant running from his house.

9. Argument of learned counsel for applicant with regard to false implication does not corroborate by any evidence as well as it does not create any doubt on prosecution story which is prima facie against applicant on the basis of eye witness account as well as statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
Thus applicant prima facie has committed a serious offence of rape which is not an offence against one an individual only but against society.

Prayer for bail, therefore,
is rejected.

10. However, the application is disposed of with direction to Trial Court to record statement of victim, if not already recorded, within a period of six months from today, if there is no other legal impediment.
Thereafter applicant is at liberty to file fresh application for bail before Trial Court.
